dispositions.reason: The proposed no-hard-delete, deactivate/reactivate, and audited-merge policy is explicitly awaiting product-owner confirmation. Current canonical material documents destructive product, membership, registration, and change-request operations, but establishes no customer-record lifecycle contract; the source snapshot contains no owning API/schema implementation or regression test for this proposed policy.

Exactly-one product_customer creation, relationship backfill, and access-revocation retention are proposed product-policy changes, not verified current behavior. The current access contract instead names active class_kit.users product membership activation for open/invite-only products; it does not establish a product_customers record or the requested backfill semantics.

The source explicitly frames separate customer and application-access resources, plus explicit audited ghost linking, as an in-flight design proposal. Current API maps document management.users and access-user administration, but do not define a separate customer resource or merge/link protocol; the proposal cannot be promoted from incidental naming alone.

Current authentication and authorization documentation establishes global auth.users with product-scoped membership and origin isolation, but it does not establish the proposed manager-discovery, disclosure, or cross-product linking rule. This privacy-sensitive policy needs an explicit accepted contract or implementation and regression evidence before canonical documentation can state it.

The current accepted ADR and active backend/auth documentation consistently resolve the present boundary as auth.users for global identity and class_kit.users for product membership/profile/role state. They contain no product_customers table, nullable auth_user_id contract, or customer_id-backed resource migration. The candidate's contrary session proposal is not current durable behavior in this checkout.

The same current accepted contract already documents the active product-user boundary: class_kit.users is the product membership table, product role assignments are scoped to product_id/user_id, and customer-facing access activates product membership only through the documented gates. No checked-in current source establishes the proposed nullable-auth customer model or customer_id foreign-key migration.

This is a requested product-policy decision and downstream implementation handoff, not evidence of an implemented Project Memory fact. It requires product-owner decision work before a future maintenance pass can document an accepted customer lifecycle contract.

This requests architecture/API verification and possible contract implementation. The current documentation exposes product-user management and access administration but no implemented customer-management resource, so the handoff belongs to product and engineering decision work rather than this documentation update.

This is a verification and potential implementation handoff for a privacy-sensitive identity boundary. Current canonical docs support product-scoped membership and origin isolation, but do not prove the requested cross-product discovery/linking behavior; no durable documentation change is warranted from the handoff alone.

The handoff asks to decide and implement a different customer/access identity model. The active accepted documentation instead names class_kit.users as the product membership boundary; no checked-in implementation confirms product_customers, nullable auth_user_id, or customer_id-backed registrations for promotion to Project Memory.
